source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Thank you for bringing back the foundation. This now feels considerably closer.

Before we refine the alphabet further, I want to return to one element of the VvÉ system. When reviewing our earlier work, I prefer the Hero V/second V hierarchy shown in concepts #2 and #3 (attached). The current proof does not yet seem to capture that same relationship.

Could you please present the following two alternatives?

Option 1: Produce the second V by duplicating the approved Hero V and proportionally reducing the entire copy as one object, without redrawing any part of it. It should remain a genuinely scaled Hero V while continuing to extend above the E and L.

Option 2: Begin with the identical copied-and-scaled Hero V, then apply only whatever minimal optical corrections you consider necessary for it to integrate naturally with the alphabet. It must preserve the same identity and remain elevated above the E and L.

After that, please adjust the optical spacing across the complete word. I like the visual cadence between the L–V in this proof and would use that relationship as the standard for balancing all other character pairs.

I attached the earlier concepts to clarify the Hero V/second V relationship I mean.

Thank you!

construction_alternatives: Option 1: Duplicate the approved Hero V and proportionally reduce the entire copy as one object without redrawing any part.
Option 2: Begin with the identical copied-and-scaled Hero V and apply only minimal optical corrections necessary for integration while preserving its identity.
